executiveSummary: The OT/ICS threat picture this period is elevated. Multiple government advisories cite active, high-confidence targeting of industrial controllers and OT perimeters, while several KEV additions and CISA weekly bulletins include directly exploitable OT technologies. The most urgent risks are: (1) nation-state and hacktivist activity against PLCs and internet-exposed HMIs; (2) active exploitation of MikroTik RouterOS edge devices and widely used dev/CI/CD platforms (Artifactory, GitLab) that can cascade into OT; and (3) newly disclosed, high-severity OT/IIoT vulnerabilities (PLC stacks, EVSE, drives, OPC UA). Active targeting of Siemens S7 PLCs with AI-assisted scripts for S7comm read/write on TCP/102; immediate removal of internet exposure and S7 protocol hardening is advised. Security Advisory Pro-Russia hacktivists are opportunistically accessing internet-exposed VNC on HMIs across Water/Wastewater, Energy, and Food/Agriculture, manipulating setpoints and alarms. Security Advisory Iranian-affiliated actors have exploited PLCs (Rockwell, Schneider, Siemens) by modifying logic/AOIs and disabling shutdown/alarm logic; disconnect PLCs from the internet and validate ladder logic integrity. Security Advisory MikroTik RouterOS is under active exploitation via unauthenticated SSH/auth bypass chains; patch immediately, restrict management, and rebuild if compromise is suspected. CERT Polska SANS ISC Active exploitation of JFrog Artifactory and GitLab can yield administrative control and secret exfiltration, enabling artifact poisoning and CI/CD supply-chain compromise that may bridge into OT environments. View Article View Article CISA weekly bulletins highlight directly exploitable OT/IIoT issues: Delta PLC Modbus exposures, EV chargers (OCPP/WebSocket RCE), Danfoss iC7 drive update/unsigned code risks, Eclipse Milo OPC UA flaws, and IIoT Arrowhead/Ditto auth-bypass/SSRF. relevance: The period's highest-confidence intelligence centers on direct manipulation or pre-positioning against industrial controllers and operator interfaces (S7 PLC families; VNC-exposed HMIs), and exploitation of OT perimeters (edge routers, SATCOM terminals) and development infrastructure (artifact repositories, SCM/CI). Several CISA bulletins name PLC/IIoT vulnerabilities with unauthenticated RCE/DoS exposure, and multiple multi-agency advisories describe active adversary TTPs against water/wastewater and energy operations. Collectively, these substantiate a HIGH threat level for OT environments with weak perimeter hygiene, flat networks, or internet-exposed assets.

descriptions: Internet scanning and access to exposed PLC/HMI services (S7comm TCP/102; VNC 5900-5910) - TA0043 / T1595.
Living-off-the-land in Windows AD/Entra ID and cloud (from CISA red-team water-sector report) - multiple enterprise TTPs.
Edge-device exploitation and persistence via rogue admin users (RouterOS) - T1136 / T1098.
Supply-chain CI/CD compromise (Artifactory/GitLab) for artifact poisoning and secret theft - T1195 / T1552.
Email platform exploitation for credential/session theft (Zimbra XSS) - T1539 / T1550.
Use of residential/SOHO botnets and covert networks to mask origin - AA26-113a patterning.

outlook72h: Block external access to S7comm and VNC; validate S7 logic integrity on internet-exposed or recently scanned assets; enforce PLC protection levels. Patch MikroTik RouterOS fleet; search for IOC users ("ops", unknown admins), scheduler scripts, and unusual SSH logs; rebuild compromised devices. Emergency changes to CI/CD: patch Artifactory/GitLab, rotate tokens/keys, and verify artifact signatures before promotion to OT staging/production. Apply OT-focused compensating controls for EVSE, drives, OPC UA servers; deploy ICS-aware IDS signatures and tighten firewall rules. For Zimbra: apply fixes and revoke app-specific passwords; monitor outbound DNS/HTTPS anomalies from email infrastructure.
